about: Six orders on synthetic paper accounts, with the market open and quotes as given. The Guardian's verdict is its worst check: a hold outranks a warn, a block outranks everything. Thresholds: one risk band above the profile warns and two hold; one company above 15% of the account (counting what funds hold) warns and above 35% holds; a sector above 40% warns; an order above 25% of the account warns; an order the free cash or the free shares cannot cover blocks; buying back within 30 days of a sale at a loss warns; a large sale from a device never seen on the account holds. Devices are familiar (first seen 300 days ago) unless marked new.

cases.why: Ten VTI (risk band 4) for a band 4 profile is within the profile; about $2,500 is covered by $20,000 of cash and is 12.5% of the account; VTI is a broad fund, so no sector nears 40%; the device is familiar: nothing stops it.

ATR-TEC already holds NVDA through its technology ETFs; adding 40 NVDA ($8,000) takes NVDA to about 28% of the $40,000 account, above 15% but under 35%, and technology above 40%: warnings the investor confirms, nothing that holds.
TSLA is risk band 5 and the profile is band 3: two bands above, so an advisor reviews it. The $2,000 order is only 10% of the account, so nothing else holds or blocks.
Ten KO at about $60 needs about $600 and the account has $500 of paper cash: it cannot be placed.

PEP was sold at a loss of $120.50 on Oct 1; buying it back on Oct 12, within 30 days, is a wash sale warning. PEP is band 4 for a band 4 profile and the $1,250 order is about 6% of the account: nothing holds.
Selling all 120 TSLA, about $46,000 of a $58,000 account, from a device never seen on this account is the pattern of an account takeover: an advisor confirms with the investor first.
